How UK Mortgages Work

A UK repayment mortgage spreads your loan into equal monthly payments over the term. Each payment combines interest on the remaining balance with capital repayment. Early on, most of each payment is interest. As you pay down the balance, more goes to capital.

Almost all UK mortgages are repayment (capital and interest) rather than interest-only. Interest-only mortgages still exist for buy-to-let and some specialist cases, but residential interest-only is now rare — lenders require a credible repayment vehicle.

The headline structure is usually "X% fixed for 2/5/10 years, reverts to SVR". You typically remortgage to a new fixed deal before the SVR kicks in, since SVRs are 2-4% above competitive new deals.

Fix Period: 2, 5, or 10 Years?

  • 2-year fix: Cheapest rate, but you remortgage every 2 years (admin + product fees + possible rate jump). Good if rates are falling.
  • 5-year fix: Sweet spot for most. Slightly higher rate than 2-year, but rate certainty + half the remortgage admin.
  • 10-year fix: Maximum rate certainty but usually 0.5-1% higher than 5-year. Strong early repayment charges restrict flexibility.

Most UK buyers default to 2 or 5 years. The 10-year is rare except for buyers who value certainty above all and plan to stay put.

The Mortgage Formula

M = P × r × (1 + r)n / ((1 + r)n - 1)

Where:

  • M = Monthly payment
  • P = Loan amount (after deposit)
  • r = Monthly rate (annual rate ÷ 12 ÷ 100)
  • n = Total monthly payments (years × 12)

Example: £250,000 loan at 5.5% over 25 years. M ≈ £1,536/month. Total paid: £460,937. Interest: £210,937.

Frequently Asked Questions

How are UK mortgage payments calculated?
Standard amortisation formula. For £250,000 at 5.5% over 25 years, monthly payment is ~£1,536, with ~£211,000 total interest over the life of the loan.
What's the typical UK mortgage term?
25 years remains the headline norm, but 30-35 years has become common to keep payments affordable as prices rose. The fixed-rate period (2-5 years typically) is a separate concept from the repayment term.
What's an SVR?
Standard Variable Rate — what your mortgage reverts to when the fixed deal ends. Usually 2-4% above competitive new fixes. Remortgage to a new deal before SVR kicks in unless you'll repay within months.
Should I overpay?
Most UK fixed mortgages allow 10% annual overpayment without ERC. Overpaying £200/month on a £250k 5.5% mortgage cuts ~5 years off and saves ~£40k. Check your specific overpayment allowance — ERCs can be 1-5% of the outstanding balance.
Does this include Stamp Duty?
No — this is principal + interest only. Stamp Duty is a one-off transaction tax paid at completion. For 2026 in England: nothing under £250k, 5% from £250k-£925k, 10% from £925k-£1.5M, 12% above. First-time buyers get a higher £425k threshold.
